name: Gulian Crommelin Verplanck
bio: Gulian Crommelin Verplanck (1786–1870) is represented in this archive by verse from Burton E. Stevenson's anthology Poems of American History (1908; revised 1922).

Poems of American History gathers verse on events from the Norse voyages to the Spanish-American War, arranged by historical chapter. The poem here is “Prophecy”; Stevenson's editorial headnotes are not reproduced.

poems.title: Prophecy
poems.author: Gulian Crommelin Verplanck
poems.text:
Hail, happy Britain, Freedom's blest retreat,
Great is thy power, thy wealth, thy glory great,
But wealth and power have no immortal day,
For all things ripen only to decay.
And when that time arrives, the lot of all,
When Britain's glory, power and wealth shall fall;
Then shall thy sons by Fate's unchanged decree
In other worlds another Britain see,
And what thou art, America shall be.
